key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within minutes to hours after exposure to trigger. LOCATION: ANYWHERE on body - face, trunk, extremities, may be localized or generalized. DURATION: Individual lesions last <24 hours, but new lesions may appear for days to weeks. CHARACTER: RAISED, WHEAL-LIKE lesions that are PRURITIC (itchy). AGGRAVATING: HEAT, stress, pressure, scratching. RELIEVING: COOL compresses, antihistamines, avoiding triggers. TIMING: Lesions appear and disappear within 24 hours, but new ones may continue. SEVERITY: 3-8/10 itching, moderate to severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SEVERE ITCHING (pruritus), raised wheals with central pallor and red borders, lesions may coalesce into larger areas, may have angioedema (swelling of lips, eyes, throat). KEY POSITIVES: Raised wheals, central pallor with red borders, severe pruritus, lesions <24 hours duration. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no systemic symptoms (unless anaphylaxis), no scaling or crusting.

red_flags: Difficulty breathing or swallowing - possible anaphylaxis, call 911
Swelling of face, lips, or throat - angioedema, call 911
Severe systemic symptoms - nausea, vomiting, dizziness - possible anaphylaxis, call 911
Rash with fever and systemic symptoms - possible serious allergic reaction, call 911
Rash involving mucous membranes - possible Stevens-Johnson syndrome, needs urgent evaluation
